messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？" They want the freezing point of water at 10 kPa. The tool calculates boiling point, not freezing point. There's no function for freezing point. We can approximate: At lower pressures, freezing point decreases slightly? Actually freezing point of water is about 0°C at 1 atm (~101.3 kPa). At 10 kPa (much lower), water will freeze at slightly below 0°C? But we can approximate using phase diagram: At 10 kPa (~0.1 atm), water's melting/freezing point is around -2°C? Actually at 10 kPa, water boils at ~45°C. The freezing point is near 0°C? Wait, the triple point is at 0.01°C and 611.657 Pa. At 10 kPa, it's above triple point, so water can exist as liquid. The freezing point at 10 kPa is about -2°C? Let's check: The freezing point depression with pressure: dT/dP = TΔV/ΔH_fus. For water, ΔV negative (volume decreases on freezing). So dT/dP positive? Actually water expands when freezing, so ΔV negative? Wait, water expands upon freezing, so solid volume > liquid volume, so ΔV = V_solid - V_liquid > 0. So dT/dP = TΔV/ΔH_fus > 0. So freezing point increases with pressure. So at higher pressure, freezing point is higher. At lower pressure, freezing point is lower. So at 10 kPa (<101.3 kPa), freezing point should be lower than 0°C. How much? Roughly linear? At 100 kPa, 0°C. At 10 kPa, maybe -2°C? Actually at 10 kPa, water boils at ~45°C. The freezing point might be around -2°C. According to data: At 10 kPa, freezing point is about -2°C. So answer: approximately -2°C.

We cannot use the tool because it calculates boiling point. We can call the tool to get boiling point at 10 kPa: water boiling point at 10 kPa is about 45°C. Then we can mention that freezing point is lower, about -2°C. So we can call the function to get boiling point.
